recipes.name: Small-batch easy kimchi (Mak-kimchi: 막김치)
recipes.yield: About ½ gallon of kimchi, plus a small plateful to serve fresh
ingredients: 2 tablespoons glutinous rice flour (sweet rice flour) or all-purpose flour
1 ounce onion (about ¼ cup), cut into chunks
3 ounces Asian pear (about ½ cup), peeled and cut into chunks
1 cup gochu-garu (Korean hot pepper flakes), or to taste
6 ounces Korean radish or daikon, peeled and cut into matchsticks
1 ounce carrot (about ¼ cup), cut into matchsticks
3 ounces buchu (Asian chives), cut into ½-inch pieces
Toasted sesame seeds, for serving fresh kimchi (optional)
instructions: Cut the cabbage lengthwise into quarters and remove the core from each quarter.
Cut each quarter in half lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 1½-inch pieces.
Transfer the cabbage to a large bowl.
Add the kosher salt and 1 cup of water and toss well. Let stand for 2 hours, tossing the cabbage every 30 minutes so it salts evenly.
Meanwhile, combine the flour and 1 cup water in a small saucepan and stir well.
Cook over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture begins to bubble, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the sugar and reduce the heat to medium. Continue stirring until the mixture becomes slightly translucent, about 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and let it cool completely.
Combine the fish sauce, cooled flour porridge, saeujeot, garlic, ginger, onion, and pear in a food processor. Process until smooth, then transfer the mixture to a large bowl.
Add the gochu-garu and stir well with a wooden spoon. Stir in the radish, carrot, chives, green onions, and oysters (if using). Mix well with a wooden spoon.
Rinse and drain the salted cabbage 3 times under cold running water. Drain thoroughly and gently squeeze out any excess water.
Add the cabbage to the seasoning mixture. Wearing disposable gloves if you like, gently mix by hand until every piece is evenly coated.
Transfer the kimchi to one or more glass jars or airtight containers. Press it down firmly to remove air pockets and pack it tightly, then cover.
You can serve the kimchi immediately, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds.

To ferment it slowly, refrigerate it for about 2 weeks. For faster fermentation, leave it at room temperature for 1 to 2 days, depending on the warmth of your kitchen, until it smells and tastes pleasantly sour. Then store it in the refrigerator.

The kimchi will continue to ferment and become more sour over time. You can enjoy it at every stage! Whenever you take kimchi from the container, press the remaining kimchi down with a spoon so it stays covered in its juices and is exposed to as little air as possible.
